A campaign launched by the Seljuk Sultan Alp Arslan against Georgia.
In 1064, Sultan Alp Arslan captured the Akhalkalaki fortress, carrying out the first successful Seljuk Turks invasion of southern Georgia. In response, the Georgians raided Arran in 1067. This triggered Alp Arslan's second invasion of Georgia in 1068. During the six-week campaign, Alp Arslan conducted successful operations in central and central-western Georgia, capturing a number of fortresses. In 1068, Sultan Alp Arslan penetrated deep into Georgia, conquering Kakheti, amassing significant spoils, and bringing the country under his control.
